how: The index drifted for three months, then fell 16.8% in eleven sessions from 22 July.
The deal did not stop the selling; attention moved to the credit rating and to Europe.
Close 1200.07. The index fell another 8.4% to the October low.

t: First session after the US downgrade: −6.7%
how: S&P cut the US to AA+ on Friday evening 5 August. Close 1119.46; VIX 48.0, its high for the decline; SPY volume 3.1 times average.

t: Fed: low rates “at least through mid-2013”
how: S&P 500 +4.7% to 1172.53 after an intraday low of 1101.54.

t: Europe bans short selling of banks; S&P 500 +4.6%
how: The fourth move of more than 4% in four sessions: −6.7%, +4.7%, −4.4%, +4.6%.

t: Retest of the August low holds: 1123.82
how: Two closes within 0.4% of the 8 August close. An eight-week range followed.
And −3.2% the next session. Policy help was sold eight sessions before the low.
1.8% under the August low with the VIX at 45.5 against 48.0. A third of the study’s stocks were at 52-week lows.
The index fell 2.2% under the prior close and finished at 1123.95.
Eleventh session after the low. The first rally since 1971 to reach a 50-day high before producing one.
Close 1284.59, 16.9% above the low. Lost again two sessions later.
5.4% above the October close after a 9.8% pullback. VIX 34.5.

t: Central banks cut the price of dollar loans; +4.3%
how: Six central banks lowered the cost of dollar swap lines. Close 1246.96.

t: ECB announces three-year loans to banks
how: S&P 500 −2.1% that day. The first loans were allotted on 21 December; bank funding stress eased in January.
